subject.title: [Bug]: claude-cli backend SIGKILLs entire process tree at turn end — Workflow / background tool orphans have no opt-out

question: Should claude-cli turn-end cleanup stay fail-closed by default, or should OpenClaw add a bounded defer-on-background-children mode plus telemetry for Workflow/native background work?
rationale: The evidence confirms the cleanup path, but changing it alters process-lifecycle guarantees, config surface, and orphan-cleanup safety rather than applying a purely mechanical fix.

options.title: Add bounded detection and opt-in defer
options.body: Add process-tree/background-child telemetry first, then allow a capped opt-in defer mode only when pending native background work is detected and live proof covers the Workflow path.

options.title: Telemetry only for now
options.body: Keep turn-end cleanup fail-closed, but log and surface killed descendants so operators and the model can see the failure instead of treating it as silent success.

options.title: Document unsupported background survivorship
options.body: Declare that Claude CLI native background work must finish before final output under OpenClaw-managed turns and route durable jobs through exec/process or cron-owned runners.

recommendation.title: Add bounded detection and opt-in defer
recommendation.body: Add process-tree/background-child telemetry first, then allow a capped opt-in defer mode only when pending native background work is detected and live proof covers the Workflow path.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily turns on the Claude CLI live-session lifecycle contract that obviyus introduced and has recently maintained.
